title: One party ruled, but many voices lived inside it
sources: Rajni Kothari, 'The Congress System in India', Asian Survey (1964)

review.note: Written and voiced by Claude (AI voices, Kokoro), 8 Nov 2026. Not yet checked by a subject or Hindi editor. Check every number and date against the listed sources.

lines.say: For two decades after independence, Congress won almost everything.
Yet India was not a one-party state.

data.headline: The party system: the Congress system

beats.say: For two decades after independence, Congress won almost everything. Yet India was not a one-party state.

lines.say: Rajni Kothari called it the Congress system.
One dominant party of consensus, with opposition parties pressing from the margins.

data.text: A party of consensus, with a margin of pressure from outside.

lines.say: In 1967, Congress lost power in several states. In 1977, the Janata Party formed the first non-Congress government at the Centre.
From 1989, coalitions became the norm for 25 years.
